transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Americans are deciding 35 U.S. Senate seats in this year's midterms.
Twenty-one are considered safe or solid.
The South Carolina seat long held by Senator Lindsey Graham until his death in July leans
Republican and new polling indicates it is vulnerable.
President Trump is returning to South Carolina today to rally for the GOP nominee, the late
senator's younger sister.
David Wasserman of the Cook Political Report is following this race.
Darlene Graham, who was appointed to replace her brother, has been struggling in adapting
to becoming a politician.
And Annie Andrews, a pediatrician who had the airwaves to herself for a few weeks because
of a fundraising advantage, she was able to close the gap.
Now, this race is very close, but the undecided vote here leans Republican.
So it's always going to be very difficult in a racially polarized state for a Democrat
to get to 50 percent.
David Wasserman speaking with NPR's Morning Edition.
Meanwhile, Vice President J.D. Vance makes an appearance today at a midterm rally in
Texas, the side of another close race.
Recent polls show Republicans, State Attorney General Ken Paxson in a dead heat with Democratic
state lawmaker James Talarico.
Latino voters in Arizona could be key in some close congressional races.
Democrats hope frustration with the economy and immigration enforcement could help them
flip at least two seats.
More from NPR's Ashley Lopez.
Latino voters helped Republicans win a slew of races in Arizona in 2024.
Jaime Malera is a Republican lobbyist in the Phoenix area, and he says many of those voters
were hoping the party would lower prices and secure the border.
But Malera says the way in which the Trump administration has carried out its policies
has since turned off a lot of those Latino voters.
I think there was a lot of agreement that there should be some strong enforcement that
takes place.
But to go in and to go into communities and just rip out individuals, I think that's left
a bad taste in a lot of Latinos' mouths.
Malera said Republicans will have to do a lot of work to win many of those voters back
before the next election cycle.
Ashley Lopez, NPR News.
The administration will allow compounding pharmacies to make six popular peptides that were previous
sleep and details from NPR's Sydney Lepkin.
The Department of Health and Human Services said in a new policy that it will use its
enforcement discretion to allow production of the peptides by compounding pharmacies.
That means regulators will look the other way, even though the peptides haven't been
rigorously tested or approved by the Food and Drug Administration.
In July, a panel of advisors to the FDA voted in favor of expanded access to the six peptides
through compounding pharmacies.
However, at the same meeting, FDA's own scientists recommended against unwinding the existing
restrictions on them.
HHS says the new policy is a safer alternative to the illicit research-use-only peptides
that consumers use now.
Sydney Lepkin and PR News.
This is NPR.
A hearing is scheduled today on whether New York Attorney General Letitia James should
be allowed to lead a criminal investigation into an alleged 2024 gang rape at Cornell.
Attorneys for two of the men named in the accuser's lawsuit argue James' social media
post reflects bias and that she should be disqualified.
However, James' office says the challenge has no merit.
This is one of at least two cases in which the state AG's neutrality has come into question.
The Democrat has also led prominent cases against Republican President Donald Trump and
Democratic former governor Andrew Cuomo.
It's turning into a tough day for technology shares on Wall Street after Alphabet, the
parent company of Google, announced earnings that missed expectations.
NPR's Rafael Noem reports that setting off new fears about artificial intelligence.
It's becoming a familiar story.
Not only did Alphabet report earnings that disappointed investors, it also said it would
continue investing massive amounts of money into developing AI, including building data
centers.
And once again, that set off concerns about whether all this spending can be sustained,
especially as competition remains intense in the AI sector.
To stay ahead, top AI companies continue to raise money.
Just this week, Anthropic announced it was pursuing a listing in the stock markets later
this year, the Nasdaq composite, which has a big share of technology shares, was hit
especially hard.
Rafael Noem, NPR News.
The Nasdaq is down 350 points.
It's NPR.
